correctness.rationale: Definitions, graph LCF normalization, cubic edge boundary identity, complement-quotiented partition count, and component-cycle criterion are explicit. verify_cuts.cpp sweeps all 8,388,607 unordered nontrivial cuts; verify_independent.cpp independently computes all 16,777,216 boundaries using a recurrence and DSU components and proves exact equality of canonical cut masks. Every eight-edge side is connected. Degree profiles, paths after suppressing degree-two vertices, cycle counts (7:32 and 8:34), Aut(G)=32, and all 21 orbit sizes are checked by verify_orbits.py against complete embedded certificates. The proof is finite, complete and deterministic; it does not extrapolate or claim independent review.

originality.rationale: The claim is the complete *eight*-edge cycle-separating cut profile (362 cuts, component topologies, 21 automorphism orbits), which is neither the known 7-edge minimum nor an ordinary connected-cut count. The published minimum-connectivity theorem covers only cuts of cardinality seven here. Generic cyclic-connectivity algorithms return the minimum size but do not determine this next layer. Full relevant sections of the strongest known cage source were materially read; exact alias, parameter, and database checks revealed no claim implying the eight-edge classification. Lack of retrieval is not treated as a guarantee of priority.

value.rationale: Cyclic edge-connectivity is a classical structural invariant of cubic cages, and the first excess-one cut layer has natural motivation as near-minimal separator stability. The claim classifies the complete eight-edge layer of the unique (3,7)-cage, separating 34 C8 cuts, 224 one-leaf enlargements, and 104 genuinely higher-cycle-core cuts (80 theta and 24 balanced K4 subdivisions), with a nontrivial AA/AB/BB classification and 21 symmetry orbits. Unlike a textbook deduction of the minimum, this information is not supplied by known minimum-cut theorems; it gives a reusable exact testbed for cubic-cage multipoles. It is restricted to the specified finite graph without unsupported general extrapolation.
